method: I describe the implemented method as known Huber iteratively reweighted least squares (IRLS), with no novelty claim. Add an intercept: A=[1,X] and B=[1,X_prediction]. Initialize beta_0=argmin_beta ||y-A beta||_2^2 using numpy.linalg.lstsq with rcond=None. The selected configuration in snapshots/initial_full/config.json is method=huber_irls, iterations=20, delta=1.345, scale=residual_mad, scale_floor=1e-8. For t=0,...,19, compute r_i=y_i-(A beta_t)_i, s_t=max(median_i|r_i-median_j(r_j)|/0.6744897501960817,1e-8), and c_t=1.345 s_t. Set w_i=1 when |r_i|<=c_t and w_i=c_t/|r_i| otherwise. Solve beta_(t+1)=argmin_beta sum_i w_i(y_i-(A beta)_i)^2 by least squares on sqrt(w_i)A_i and sqrt(w_i)y_i. Return B beta_20. These weights correspond to Huber loss rho(u)=u^2/2 for |u|<=1.345 and rho(u)=1.345|u|-1.345^2/2 otherwise, with residual scale recomputed at each iteration. The code uses exactly 20 updates without a convergence stopping criterion.
limitations: I read the recorded metrics; I did not independently reproduce the experiments. The selected method has mean full-validation MSE 0.04132739672516235 on seeds 0–4, versus baseline 1.99069057153675; its subset-validation MSE is 0.048565701283490234. These are validation results used in candidate comparison, not held-out test evidence. The additional run on seeds 10–14 reports full-validation MSE 0.04058449520270195 and explicitly has extra=true: it is extra-seed validation, not independent held-out testing. No matched extra-seed baseline appears in the supplied metrics, so that run alone cannot establish a comparative improvement on those seeds. Five seeds per run and aggregate MSE do not establish broad robustness or statistical significance. Known Huber IRLS on synthetic data does not establish scientific novelty or real-world generalization. Residual downweighting does not guarantee robustness to high-leverage feature contamination. The fixed iteration count does not certify convergence, and recomputing the residual scale does not justify claiming minimization of one fixed-scale Huber objective. The metrics alone do not establish runtime, memory efficiency, universal component necessity, or optimality.
